To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a learning agent can learn the decomposition of composite sequential tasks, (2) the learning algorithm is computationally efficient, (3) it achieves transfer of learning, and (4) it is robust to the presence of noise.

(1) the learning agent learns to solve a class of complex sequential decision tasks by composing solutions of elemental sequential decision problems, and (2) the solution of a complex sequential decision task is constructed by a computationally inexpensive modification of the solutions of elemental sequential tasks.

(i) a new algorithm can be used to transfer learning across composite tasks by sharing the solutions to elemental tasks, (ii) the algorithm is provably correct, and (iii) the algorithm can be implemented in a modular architecture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: Can we build agents that are more efficient in solving a set of tasks than an agent that solves the tasks separately?
the transfer of learning by composing solutions of elemental sequential decision problems.
the following questions: How can a learning agent learn to solve multiple sequential decision tasks?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper provides a novel and effective approach for solving composite sequential decision tasks that is based on the transfer of learning.
the learning agent learns to solve a set complex tasks with a small number of elemental SDTs, by learning the structure of the tasks and by sharing the solutions across the tasks.
the proposed learning algorithm and architecture can achieve transfer of learning by composing solutions of elemental sequential tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the learning agent learns the decomposition of SDTs, learns the solution of the elemental SDTs, and uses these solutions to solve the composite SDTs.
a learning agent can solve complex tasks by solving simpler tasks, which is an instance of the principle that complex systems are constructed by combining simpler systems.
we present a new learning architecture for solving composite sequential tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transfer of learning can be achieved by sharing the solutions across multiple SDTs.
the transfer of learning across multiple tasks can be achieved by composing solutions of elemental tasks.
learning to solve multiple tasks can be done more efficiently by learning a decomposition of the tasks into simpler tasks.
